[justify][author]\033WTutorial[/author]\033WPassengers will automatically get onboard your ship when you dock at stations. Their destination will be displayed on the Passenger manifest or inside their ware info panel, accessible from your Freight Bay. The payment you'll receive is based on the distance you travel. A higher reputation means that your clients will trust you to travel farther.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033GAutomatic Delivery System[/author]Hello %s,

You have \033C{1}\033X object waiting for you. It was previously owned by %s and has been automatically transferred to your cargo bay. Good day!

\033WYou have acquired a Data Scanner. This device allows you to scan any ship in order to unlock its blueprint to your future Outposts. Data scanning is a safe and free process. To start scanning a ship, you must first assign a special hotkey from the Control settings menu, at the bottom of the Interface tab. Scanning takes some time and to unlock a blueprint, you often requires multiple scans on different ships of the same type. It can be a tedious task, but you'll soon be able to make the process faster by building Research stations in your sectors.[/justify]

[author]\033YVincentTH[/author]
[center]\033YWelcome to Mayhem 3 Renegades.[/center]


[justify]\033WPlease set up these hotkeys in Options > Controls > Interface

- Personal console
- Data Scanner
- Experimental Transporter

Mayhem is focused on empire building and dynamic territorial warfare.

Territory control constantly shifts over time. Difficult situations may occur, but the game should never soft-lock player progression.

Factions that become too powerful will eventually face coalitions formed by smaller factions.

Defeating the OCV is optional, unlike in Litcube's Universe.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou are not allowed to dock to the Outposts of other factions.\n\nThe only way to interact are commands like Trade:Trade Run or Worker:Trader.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WCargo Hauler offers jobs when you dock to random stations of your choice. The payment you'll receive is based on the distance that you travel. A higher reputation makes your clients trust you to go further.\n\nSometimes you will receive job offers for illegal cargo. This will be displayed in your Freight menu. Successful illegal shipments also create new opportunities to sell Space Weed.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYour Outpost can produce ships and stations, congratulations!

You should set up this hotkey in game options: [yellow]Controls > Interface > Outposts[/yellow]

\033WBuy more food so that your people will not starve and can generate free resources and tax income which gets better over time.

Additional perk slots can be unlocked later by using the "Adjacency Bonus" perk, Terraforming, or upgrading to a Capital Shipyard.

Useful first factories are often a Solar Power Plant paired with a Satellite factory and then selling the satellites.

Use your starting resources wisely. They might not last to build a self sufficient economy. Don't be afraid to buy resources. A factory will run for hours even from a single resource delivery.

Tip: don't use automated Traders until you have a small fleet to hunt down pirates. Alternatively get some infamy so that they leave your ships mostly alone.

Good luck![/justify]

[justify][author]\033GCommonwealth Identity Control[/author]Message to %s
Object: IMPORTANT
Date: %s

During routine maintenance, a database error occurred while updating your profile. This automatic identity control process is necessary to ensure that your personal data has not been compromised. You can navigate this menu using your keyboard.

\033WNote: Some lag or stuttering may occur during the first ten minutes of the game, even after galaxy generation.
Reminder: Please read the in-game Encyclopedia. For information about ship commands, press 'i' when highlighting a command. Many gameplay values can be edited in 9972-L044.xml and 9973-L044.xml.[/justify]

[author]\033GCommonwealth Identity Control[/author][white]Higher difficulties introduce additional modifiers. Insane adds further modifiers beyond Hard and skips the remaining setup questions. On Easy, the AI cannot attack the player unprovoked, tax income is extremely generous, and sectors have no upkeep.

[/white][red]Hard[/red] and [magenta]Insane[/magenta][white]:[/white]
- Sectors and Jump Beacons cost upkeep.
- Player Jump Beacons have limited placement and can be deployed only in friendly or unclaimed sectors.
- Renegades use larger ships.
- Fewer unclaimed sectors remain after your first conquest.
- Bailed ships retain fewer lasers and shields.
- War declarations are more likely.
- Some OCV fleets can deep strike farther from Xenon sectors.

[author]\033GCommonwealth Identity Control[/author]Congratulations! Your personal database is now up to date.

[justify][author]\033RUnknown[/author]My name is Niklas, you don't know me. I'm contacting you on behalf of your father. Before he passed away, he asked me to meet you in person and give you a precious device he spent the last decade to obtain. Unfortunately, the situation has worsened since I last spoke with him. Each faction is now fighting for obscure reasons and everyone seems to forget who the real enemy is. But I digress, this is not our subject.

This device is now in the hands of the government and unlike these guys, I belong to a group that honour the traditions and the memories of the %ss. I won't lie: we work against them and we have fought them for decades. Believe it or not, your father was one of us. I will send you a page of his personal diary for you to forge your own opinions. If you think we are right to fight for our freedom and independence, and if you want to join us, you will have to prove your worth. Whatever your ambition is, make your mark on this galaxy, complete your Ascension, and we'll talk again soon.

\033WThe Ascension is a set of goals that you can follow in the dedicated section of your Personal console.[/justify]

[text cols='1' colwidth='400'][justify]\033YThe following text is an encrypted excerpt from a book written 16 years ago

\033X... on my way here. The most important thing to remember is that history is never with us, the people. The bad guys always win and they tell their children what they want to hear. Obedience doesn't make men, free will does. You have to read between the lines and accept the truth without looking back on your actions. That's what this rebellion is about: understanding the world without fear, tears or laughters. Do you think that Terracorp pities us? Can you imagine them approving a plan that would make them less important in this galaxy? Or maybe you have been fed on sweet lies and illusions. Then let me refresh your memory on the past...

As you probably know from school, the Terrans started the terraforming of thousands of planets centuries ago. In their desperate attempt to control everything, they built an AI capable of doing the hard work, the Xenon, who later turned against their people. What you don't know however is that the Commonwealth tried to fight the Xenon, but instead of helping them, the Terrans declared war on them because of their mad scientists believing that some Xenon were still active and working in the interest of their ruthless empire.

After five consecutive wars, the Commonwealth was defeated. Each faction, the Argons, the Borons, the Paranids, the Splits and the Teladis were banned from the core galaxies. For many years, they hid in the dark corners of the known universe, while the Terrans were creating Terracorp, a giant company that will be used to deal with the "outside problems". From this day, everything was made private and the Terrans managed to influence the people to believe that they were unimpeachable.

Some years later, they had this idea of terraforming new planets... They didn't imagine how strong the Xenon had become over the time, and Terracorp stole billions of credits in taxes to send Terrans to their death against these vicious machines. But then, the desire for more profits made them change their minds. Instead of sending more military ships to the galaxies controlled by the Xenon, they auctioned these sectors to the remnant of the Commonwealth, making them believe that they could rise again and become the strong factions they always wanted to be. The core sectors would still be closed to them and they will always stay at the edge of the conquered universe, but they were free to exist and they wouldn't have to hide anymore. They accepted the offer and bought hundreds of galaxies infested with Xenon. Of course, this threat was hidden from them by the Terrans. What they did tell them however was that Terracorp was in charge of these outer border galaxies. Some rules were designed to limit the expansion of each faction. Obviously, this lead to internal wars, and without leaders able to reunite everyone, we stood no chance against the Terrans. We had to deal with the cupidity and the thirst for power on one side, and the Xenon on the other side...

\033YEnd of the excerpt[/justify][/text]

[justify][author]\033G%s Notary Office[/author]%s,

A recent document signed by your father has reached us this morning. Because you are his only legitimate heir, we managed to add this object to the list of his last wishes. Please dock to the station %s in the sector %s. I will upload the location to your personal journal. The object is sealed but its digital signature indicates that it has been registered as a scanner a few years ago.

Kind regards,
%s

\033WYour personal journal differs from your message log. It can store custom entries and also automatically updates mission objectives. You can access your journal through your Personal console \(assign a hotkey or use the Additional Ship Command menu to open it\). You can also assign a hotkey directly to your journal.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033WTutorial[/author]\033WTo start your empire, you must build an Outpost that will show the other factions that you are gaining power, and that you are ready to expand your influence. Remember that in this galaxy, people are tired of war and will easily turn their loyalty to an independent empire such as yours.

To begin your journey, you have received a TL, waiting for you in %s. Unload the Outpost from its cargo bay to conquer your first sector. In this Outpost, you will find some food, basic resources, and a Research station. Try not to make new enemies and prefer an Unknown sector in a quiet area, and make sure no pirates or Xenon are around. Be careful though, factions that are in adjacent sectors won't like the fact that you settle too close to them. However, for this time, they should ignore you.

This new TL is maintenance-free, but the others you will build yourself will be at your own expense.

\You can unload a station if you are in a different sector by using the Remote Drop Station command, available in the Special section of your TL.

In the TL, you will also find some Jump Beacons. Use them wisely. If you want to build more Jump Beacons, please read the Mechanics -> Jump Beacons section of the encyclopedia; or read the information panel from your TL's Freight Bay.[/justify]

[justify]You have the TL, good. There is an Outpost in its cargo bay; use it to conquer your first sector. Try not to make new enemies and prefer an Unknown sector over a crowded one. Be careful though, factions that are in adjacent sectors won't like the fact that you settle so close to them, but at this point we don't really have a choice.\n\nWhile you're doing this, we are preparing some direct actions against our enemies. They will soon learn that they should have respected the people.[/justify]

[justify]You don't know who I am, but we know who you are; or at least, we know who your father was. I am working for an independent corporation that has been watching you for quite some time now.\n\nI've managed to get my hands on the quantum device your "group" is looking for. It was unsecured and nobody knows what it is anyway. Your father knew however, and we know from his personal database that this tool can help you to go from a sector to another faster than anyone else in this galaxy. I'm willing to sell it to you for 100,000 credits. I'm the only one to know about this, so if you're interested, come to %s with the money and I'll hand it over to you.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OCommonwealth Old News Network[/author]Time of dispatch: %s\n\nThis morning, another group of Xenon has been spotted in the sector %s, where the machines are gathering to destroy our assets. This old network is already being hacked by government entities to try to cut us off from telling the truth. We must act now and stop our internal wars in order to face the Xenon and the Terrans who are responsible for their creation. This will probably be the last and only message we'll be able to send. We need help to destroy the Xenon [u]stations[/u] in the hope of slowing them down and maybe even stopping them completely.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033GBreaking News[/author]Dear citizens,\n\nDespite our efforts to end the war and bring peace in our galaxy, a weak and disorganized rebellion known as the Yakis has recently sabotaged several of our stations. These actions will not be tolerated and we will find and put on trial any person related to those crimes.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033GAutomatic Delivery System[/author]Hello %s,

You have \033C{2}\033X objects waiting for you. You can only unlock one. To unlock, pay %s credits.

[u]Notice: you will be prosecuted if you cause any damage to the system.[/u]

\033WThe choice you're about to make is irreversible. The Jumpdrive Prototype allows your own ship to teleport to any sector for a variable amount of Energy Cells. It has a long cooldown. On the other hand, the Experimental Transporter Device allows you, as a pilot, to teleport to any of your ship and switch place with its pilot. It doesn't cost anything and has a much shorter cooldown. Both devices are activated with the Teleportation device hotkey, and they cannot be used to transport anything else than your ship or yourself.[/justify]
Pay 100,000 credits for the Jumpdrive Prototype

[justify][author]\033GAutomatic Delivery System[/author]One message enclosed:
===================

I cannot really meet you in person, it would be too dangerous. The device you just acquired is said to be impossible to duplicate by Terracorp, and unfortunately I think they're right. I hope it will help you nonetheless, and that you will bring peace to our galaxy. Good luck![/justify]

[justify][author]\033OCommonwealth Old News Network[/author]Time of dispatch: %s

We have just intercepted several official reports confirming the loss of Xenon station signals in all Xenon sectors. Those reports are quite incomplete and somewhat cryptic in some sections, so we cannot be sure that the Xenon have all been destroyed. But for now, let's just thank the Independents for what they've done, and hope that the Xenon won't return.

\033WYou have gained some reputation with all factions, plus one Favor Point.[/justify]

[justify]You did a good job building an empire from the ground up, but as you have your priorities, we also have our own, and we now need to focus on the Commonwealth. We know you probably have some friends amongst these factions, but with your help we now have a real chance to bring peace to the galaxy and stop all corruption for good.\n\nAs your father said, these battles must be ruthless. We have several people dedicated to the sabotage of their assets. Thanks to that and our influence, we have taken control of a small part of this galaxy, and we are getting stronger every hour. You have your own force now; whether or not you want to help us is up to you.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OCommonwealth Old News Network[/author]Time of dispatch: %s

The following is a confidential report from one of the Commonwealth faction whose name will remain hidden.

"A few days ago, me and Professor Liam have witnessed a rift in space-time. As we were starting to celebrate our new discovery - a new way to gather our ships from distant galaxies - we realized that the signal we received from what we call "the Maelstrom" was not from any known factions. It first looked like the signature of several Xenon ships, because we know that the Terrans have built thousands of them and it definitely not human-controlled, but then we took a closer look and managed to identify one single ship. Then a few hours ago we opened another rift from which hundreds of those signals were passing through.

Addendum: after another failure, we've decided to abandon our project. It seems that the calibration is wrong and we cannot identify the galaxies we are targeting. These new machines seem to have been left there for a reason, with no way to escape. Hopefully, the rifts we opened are now closed and they won't get through."[/justify]
[justify][author]\033GBreaking News[/author]The Commonwealth is now installing Advanced Firewall Softwares and Internal Sentry Lasers on most of their ships to protect their assets.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033REmergency Channel[/author]Dear citizens,\n\nMy name is Professor Liam and I'm working for the Commonwealth Intergalactic Observatory. We have noticed a rift in the space-time continuum in %s. That is probably nothing to worry about as we currently are doing our best to close it, but you must keep away from it. We have strong reasons to believe that this could help ships from other galaxies to come in, but the other way remains inexplicably closed. In other words: you cannot go through. So please stay away and let us do our work.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033CCommonwealth Council[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,\n\nTo guarantee the peace amongst our galaxy, we have decided that every organization, faction, or any group of any sort that were not cooperative towards our respectable goal, especially regarding our position on the Yakis situation, would be considered not worthy of our gratitude. Please see this symbolic gesture as a way for you to make the right choices in the future.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033GBreaking News[/author]Dear citizens!

It's a great day today, as the OCV portals have all just vanished from our galaxy! Our scientists are still not able to explain this phenomenon, nor deny if whether or not it is permanent, but they seem to be rather confident and full of hope for our future. They've also managed to extract precious data from the OCV ships.

\033WCongratulations, you have defeated the OCV in this galaxy! As a reward, you can now research all OCV ships and build their lasers.[/justify]
[justify]I knew we could count on you my friend! Now it's time for the Yakis to rise![/justify]
Pay 100,000 credits for the Experimental Transporter Device

[justify]You've built another Outpost, well done! Maybe it's time for us to grow stronger by increasing your fleet.\n\nThere's another way to acquire ships than just building them: you could steal the ships of other factions... If you're interested, I've got a guy in the trading station of %s that could sell you some "volunteers". With a little training, I'm sure you could make good use of them.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]Getting started:

Explore to find a nice and safe sector. It's not really helpful to place many satellites at this point.

Try to acquire about 10 ships during your Ascension. Go for Remnant signals \(Journal\) or bailed ships \(see faction claims in Ministry of War\) or the black market \(see Personal Console\)

Earn reputation with factions who might become your future neighbor. Do missions or destroy pirates in their sectors.

Bounties are profitable \(see the Bounty Board in the Personal Console\). If you manage to kill a pirate commander, his remaining group will flee from you.

You can do Cargo Hauling or Taxi jobs \(register your ship in the Personal Console\). Trading is typically not viable unless you are experienced with this mod and know which deals to look for. Most players should just wait until they can have stations which generate or produce something and then sell their output.

Try to scan a neutral trader to steal his cargo.

It's very helpful if you use the time to unlock blueprints for an M6, some fighters, a TS, and a TS miner variant \(use your Data Scanner\).[/white][/justify]

[justify][author]\033MTerracorp[/author]Dear pilot,

It is now time to discuss your future among the galaxy.

We are now giving you the ability to order a terraforming mission on the planets you control. Once an order has been given, our Terran terraformers will teleport there and start the process. During this time, some old entities that were once our first terraformers inside the Omicron Channel could be awaken and will probably attack the sector. Hold tight, defend your assets and keep an eye on the abnormal signals displayed on your galaxy map. These signals were once used to encrypt our transmissions when we were terraforming our core planets. They may be a good indication of how strong the ancient terraformers are in the sector. Also, if the signals are low, we will be able to terraform the planet faster.

\033WYou can now terraform planets in any sector you control in order to gain special bonuses. Terraforming is accessible through the Ministry of War menu.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033MTerracorp[/author]Dear pilot,

You have done a great job helping us terraforming your planets. Unfortunately, the OCV is too much of a threat in this area for us to invest more time into your installations. We leave you a team of specialists in case you would like to terraform more planets, and also a Forseti, for your trouble. Good luck.

\033WYou have received a Terran Forseti in %s.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033WTerracorp CEO[/author]Admiral,

You have succeeded in your task, congratulations! All the sectors are now owned by the Terrans, and your actions will help to calm things down with the Commonwealth. You brought a bit more peace to the galaxy!

With this galaxy finally safe, I'm sure the Terran Council will need our services again in a different galaxy! Head back to your core headquarters and prepare for your next assignment![/justify]

[justify][author]\033WTerracorp CEO[/author]Admiral,\n\nYou have failed in your task. All your Outposts have been destroyed and there is no hope in this galaxy anymore. Abort all operations and report back to your core headquarters in the next two weeks. We have other galaxies to conquer.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033GBreaking News[/author]Civil unrest! %s sectors are banding together in a massive rebellion!\n\nPiracy is thriving and insurance rates begin to soar. Our galaxy faces more instability.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033WTutorial[/author]\033WThis galaxy is young, and the factions are only beginning to expand. As a result, some rules work differently in this setting:

- Factions will begin conquering sectors before you complete your Ascension.
- The OCV will begin spawning from its main portal after 1 day.
- The Black Market unlocks after 12 hours or immediately upon reaching nation status.
- NPC squadrons behave more recklessly.
- NPC Outposts and Trading Stations start with additional resources.
- Secondary missions have less variety early on.
- Kha'ak raids begin after 1 day.
- Xenon activity is reduced for the first day.

A few tips for this game mode:

- Kha'ak presence increases with the number of asteroids in a sector. Avoid sectors with many asteroids early on.
- Hire mercenaries when you need additional firepower.
- Make use of Trading Stations.
- Minimize unnecessary risks. Kha'ak ships are fast and powerful, but sufficiently fast ships can still explore or pass through infested sectors without engaging them.
- Abandoned ships in this young galaxy are mostly Terran, as the Terran empire was the first to venture into this region. These ships are powerful, but prioritize claiming the fastest ones so you can avoid unnecessary combat.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]You have reached a Terran Memory sector.

You may find abandoned [yellow]Jump Beacons[/yellow] in these sectors. Claim them from your spacesuit or order a ship to do so using Cmd > Special > Capture Ship. A ship with sufficient cargo space is required to collect a Jump Beacon.

Jump Beacons function like gates, and your ships automatically use them when they provide a faster route. A well-designed network can connect distant sectors, improve tax efficiency, and bypass dangerous sectors.

On harder difficulties, Jump Beacons are very expensive to maintain and can be deployed only in unclaimed, friendly, or player-owned sectors. On all difficulties, the number of Jump Beacons you can own is limited, so place them only in strategically valuable locations.

The Maintenance screen displays how frequently each Jump Beacon is used, helping you evaluate its value. The most useful beacons typically have a low average jump cost and are located near the center of separated clusters of player-owned sectors or at important allied junctions.

The Jump station perk provides another way to establish direct connections between sectors. The number of Jump stations you can build is also limited.[/justify]

page.title: Script user help
page.t: All manufacturing components will be added as products into this Outpost.

This command will erase previous jobs and create news ones based on wares required to build stations and ships. A base value will be asked to determine the quantity of wares that will be setup in the Acquire jobs. All jobs created this way have Trade as target.
This ship data will be added to the database in order to research its blueprint.
Displays the mission briefing of the current station this ship is docked at, if any.

This ship will get repaired to its homebase or the nearest safe Outpost, or to its carrier if it's equipped with a Carrier Repair Module. Workers get automatically repaired, as well as fleet followers if their fleet setting allows it.

This ship will get an inspection from its homebase or the nearest safe Outpost. A ship inspection resets the maintenance factor of the ship. You can also send your ships for an inspection through the Maintenance screen. Workers get automatically maintained, as well as fleet followers if their fleet setting allows it.

This ship will build a portal to the enigmatic sector Blue Horizon. The progress will be displayed in the name of the ship and it will only advance if the ship remains in the source sector. The ship must have enough Nividium to be able to initiate this command. Works only during the main story.
Send a squad of marines to board a nearby ship.
Send a squad of marines to board a nearby ship.
Colours the name of the station.
Triggers an electromagnetic pulse that disrupt every shield in the sector.
Triggers an electromagnetic pulse that disrupt every shield in a 50km radius.

This command will start the universe trader. It will trade all wares that can be bought and sold to achieve profits. If a homebase is set, then station's money is used and the UT will stay around it, otherwise the player's money will be used and the maximum trading range will be based on the UT experience. If the ship runs out of trade opportunities it will stay on standby and try again. More experience increases profits. If the UT has a homebase, it will respect its maximum trading range setting. UT experience determines the absolute maximum trading range.\n{2022,99991}
The Crystal Transmuter is used to create new crystals from lower quality ones. Synthesized Crystals gives Red crystals, Red gives Yellow, Yellow gives Blue and so on.

This command will make the fleet commander call all ships currently with fleet to regroup at a custom rally point. Ships that are "currently not with fleet" are disregarded. If some ships can dock to your carriers, they will do so and become support ships. Your ships will protect the commander and look for optimal targets regarding their fleet settings that you can modify through your Personal console.
This command will make the ship to join up with its fleet commander and be ready for fleet orders. It will become a support ship if it can dock to in-fleet carriers.
This command will order the fleet commander to organise an attack against a single target.
This command will order the fleet commander to organise the fleet ships to kill all enemy ships found in the sector.
This command will order the fleet commander to defend the sector and keep it clear from any hostile ships.
This command will order the fleet commander to organise a defence force to protect a station or to escort a ship.
This command will order the fleet commander to organise an invasion fleet to destroy all stations in a given sector. If there are no stations left, the fleet will start defending the sector.
This command is the general behaviour of all fleet members. They will look for targets that are close to the commander, then protect the commander or attack its target.

This command will make the fleet commander and all fleet members to retreat to a nearby safe sector, if any. The maximum range at which this safe sector is from the commander can be modified in the fleet settings menu.

This command will make a ship collect missiles from your Outposts and distribute them among a specified fleet, according to the resupply options that you can edit through the weapons menu of any ship. The supplier can only be affected through the fleet settings menu, and it can be affected to multiple fleets at the same time. The supplier will keep looking for available missiles and order new ones at its homebase if possible.
This ship will tug every fighter that is coming to its homebase without being able to jump. It will also tug followers when possible.
This command will order the ship to go to your nearest jump beacon, if any.

Agents are assigned to Outposts and factories. When assigned to an Outpost, Agents will execute import and export orders from the jobs list that you can customize through the Outpost Manager menu. When assigned to a factory, Agents will import the resources that the factory needs, and export the products it produces. Priority is given to the local Outpost when importing. Agents assigned to a factory will export products to the local Outpost if there are no other clients.\n\nAgents never trade with other factions, unlike Traders.

Explorers are assigned to Outposts and Advanced Satellite Factories. Their only purpose is to deploy a network of satellites and ensure that every reachable sector is monitored. When they do not have at least one Advanced Satellite in their cargo hold, they will search their homebase, then the local Outpost. If none are available, they will wait. Explorers operate with a fixed range of 15 sectors and ignore the Maximum Sector Distance setting of their homebase. They do not purchase Satellites from other faction stations and will not map hostile sectors.

Looters are assigned to Outposts. They're continuously scanning nearby sectors for flying wares. When they find at least one, they collect it and go back home when all flying wares have been collected. They don't go in hostile sectors. Their collecting range is increased with a Transporter Device.
Miners are assigned to Outposts and Quantum Tube Fab factories. They need to be equipped with Mobile Drilling Systems. They mine debris that are local to their homebase.
Service ships are assigned to Outposts. They respond to local calls for help of various nature.

Traders are assigned to Outposts and Trading Stations. They first try to trade their homebase's wares that are listed in the Traders section of the logistics menu, in the Outpost Manager, then they look for opportunities by browsing reachable factories.\n\nIf you want to trade a ware that you have in one of your Outposts, you must explicitly add it to the list of wares in the Traders tab of the Logistics section, in the Outpost Manager menu.

Tugs are assigned to Outposts. They're continuously scanning nearby sectors for abandoned ships that bailed out. Then they capture them and bring them back to their homebase. They don't go in hostile sectors. Their claiming range is increased with a Remote System Control Software.
This ship will flee to the nearest dockable station. It will abort if no station can be found.
This ship will flee to a position.
Battle Groups invade sectors. Once a target has been chosen, the Battle Group will gather to a safe sector and start the invasion of the target from here right after claiming it.
Border Patrols defend sectors that are at the border of their territory.
Escort ships either protect freighters or defend their current sector.
Police ships chase ships that carry illegal wares onboard. They also defend their home sector and adjacent ones.
Rearguard ships defend all sectors that are not at the border of their territory.
Task Force is a special group that launches random raids over weak ships or static asset like Advanced Satellites and Jump Beacons. They also make sure that enemy attacks are not left unpunished.
Raider ships perform hit-and-run anti-logistics operations against other hostile factions by attacking enemy freighters.

Support ships are the ones that can dock into carriers, generally fighters. This command makes them defend the carrier and attack its target, if any. If the carrier is equipped with a Carrier Repair Module, the support ship will stay docked until repaired. If the carrier is destroyed, the ship will try to find another one in its current formation.
This ship will scan all asteroids in its current sector. It does not search other sectors.
This command will make the ship patrol the selected sector and defend it against all enemy ships in range. If you have an Advanced satellite in the sector, the ship range is extended.
This ship will attack all enemy ships in range. Unless the Defend Sector command, the ship will stay in position. If you have an Advanced satellite in the sector, the ship range is extended.
This ship will attack all enemy ships in range. Unless the Defend Sector command, the ship will stay in position. If you have an Advanced satellite in the sector, the ship range is extended.

Command this ship to collect a ware flying around in a sector. This ship must have enough free cargo space and a high enough transport class to carry the ware. Collecting range is increased with a Transporter Device.
Command this ship to capture an abandoned ship in a sector. Claiming range is increased with a Remote System Control Software. Cannot be called on your own ship.
Force this ship to follow your current ship. Attacks are ignored.
Force this ship to follow another ship. Attacks are ignored.
Turret command to fire at all enemies that are in the turrets firing range.\n{2022,99990}
Turret command to make the current target of the ship the primary attack target of the turret.\n{2022,99990}
Turret command to fire on attacking ships, and also shoot at incoming missiles. On M8 class ships, this can be used to protect nearby allies from all incoming missiles.\n{2022,99990}
Turret command to fire on attacking ships.\n{2022,99990}

Turret command to fire at missiles, and missiles only. Will not attempt to shoot at any ships even when under attack. On M8 class ships, this can be used to protect nearby allies from all incoming missiles\n{2022,99994}
Turret command to fire at fighters only, ignoring freighters and larger ships.\n{2022,99994}
Turret command to fire at capital ships only, ignoring freighters and fighters.\n{2022,99994}
Turret Command Alpha is a blank template for the captain to configure from the Gameplay menu.
Turret Command Beta is a blank template for the captain to configure from the Gameplay menu.
Turret Command Gamma is a blank template for the captain to configure from the Gameplay menu.
This command will order this ship to collect all wares flying around in a sector. He will return home, if any, to unload the wares he collected, or will dock to the nearest safe station.

Connects to your current target and also displays information from your hacking database. This action cannot be performed by other pilots. Like all hacking commands, this one requires a Hacking Rootkit.

Scans your current target for open ports. This scan cannot be performed by other pilots. The scan itself is secured, but requires a constant targeting connection. The target must be in a valid scanning range. Like all hacking commands, this one requires a Hacking Rootkit.

Installs a backdoor to your current target. This action costs 1 Hackerchip and cannot be performed by other pilots. The target must have a vulnerable port. The target must be in a valid scanning range. Like all hacking commands, this one requires a Hacking Rootkit.

Uploads a worm on the station you are currently docked at. This action costs 1 Hackerchip and cannot be performed by other pilots. You must have a strong botnet to be able to crack the admin password of the station public interface. Like all hacking commands, this one requires a Hacking Rootkit.

Uninstalls an existing backdoor on a specified port of your current target. This action costs 1 Hackerchip and cannot be performed by other pilots. The target must be in a valid scanning range. Like all hacking commands, this one requires a Hacking Rootkit.

Creates a product from specific resources directly from this ship. This command requires the Mobile Factory Kit, and it also requires that the ship remains still and undocked during the whole production process. Any other command that is given during this process will interrupt it and resources engaged will be lost. Note that this method of production is less efficient than a conventional factory.
Moves to the selected position and places the station there.
Repairs a ship with the Truelight Seeker.
Deploys all stations to a target sector.

page.title: Boardcomp. objects
page.t: Due to shortages of materials traditionally used to manufacture infantry equipment, scrap metal is now commonly used to produce ammunition, weapons, and gear for marines and mercenaries. Pirates are well known for their skill in creating such equipment.

The Disintegrator rifle is a common type of sidearm. It was invented by a wealthy Family member who believed his design was so perfect that the weapon would literally disintegrate everything in its path, hence the name. In reality, it is a weak rifle that can barely shoot straight. It has one advantage, though: its low cost. Disintegrator Rifles are considered highly illegal throughout most of known space, even though many marines and pirates use them on a daily basis.

Low-yield Sidearms (illegal), which include phase pistols and stun handguns, are used by many law enforcement and military forces. Their limited firepower prevents them from being used during tactical assaults and boarding operations.

Terran EMP Rifles (illegal) are widely used by Terran forces against ground vehicles and static defenses. The rifle is so large that it must be operated by a two-man team. It is effective only against electrically powered targets.
The Railgun is an electrically powered weapon specifically designed for use on Lasertowers. The weapon is so large and heavy that the entire Lasertower is built around it.

This device harnesses the remarkable properties of Black Crystals to induce molecular transformation in other crystals, transmuting them into higher-quality variants. Synthesized Crystals are also compatible. Informally known among pilots as "The Philosopher's Stone," the Crystal Transmuter has undergone several upgrades over time. The latest version can drain large amounts of shield energy to make transmutation almost instantaneous.
This high-tech equipment allows a ship to perform maintenance while in operation, preventing its maintenance factor from increasing while undocked.

This heavy equipment consists of multiple tools designed to repair docked ships over time. Although the process is slow, its advanced design allows repairs to be performed using existing materials at no additional cost.

For a long time, the device was listed as "Unknown Artifact 78642F." It was stored in a Terran factory far from the core galaxies and forgotten while the Xenon destroyed most USC assets. Terracorp recently discovered that the artifact survived the attacks, but attempts to retrieve it failed, and it has since been reported as stolen government property. Terracorp has reminded the Commonwealth that the use of quantum teleportation is strictly forbidden within the outer border galaxies. Due to the device's extremely early stage of development, all attempts to replicate it are expected to fail.
This device generates a considerable amount of energy that can be released in a rapid electromagnetic pulse, affecting the shields of all ships and structures near the emitter.

For a long time, the device was listed as "Unknown Artifact 78642F." It was stored in a Terran factory far from the core galaxies and forgotten while the Xenon destroyed most USC assets. Terracorp recently discovered that the artifact survived the attacks, but attempts to retrieve it failed, and it has since been reported as stolen government property. Terracorp has reminded the Commonwealth that the use of quantum teleportation is strictly forbidden within the outer border galaxies. Due to the advanced nature of the device, all attempts to replicate it are expected to fail.

This huge station has all the necessary infrastructure to accommodate a large population and construct new ships and stations. Originally designed by Goner architects, all Outposts are built around an ingenious system of movable walls that allows new rooms to be created as needed, making the entire station highly flexible. It also has a repair bay and a ship hangar.

Originally designed by the Terrans, this station contains all the equipment needed to research new blueprints. All Research Stations share the same database and can work simultaneously on the same project. Once a blueprint is fully researched, it can be built from any Outpost.
A specialized device that scans other ships to obtain the structural data required to research their blueprints.
Infrared and IFF-guided Internal Sentry Lasers can be installed at strategic locations aboard a ship to provide enhanced internal security against intrusion and boarding.

The Hull Polarising Device generates a powerful, sustained magnetic field around a ship's hull, severely disrupting even the most efficient plasma cutters. This provides protection against forced hull entry.
This equipment allows a ship to instantly dock at the nearest station or carrier within range. A Docking Computer is not required when docking at a carrier equipped with a Transporter Device.

Chemical Labs are large factories that turn general waste into a highly toxic liquid that is later stabilized in cold rooms. The environment in these rooms is so extreme that every Chemical Lab is fully automated. The Chemicals produced here are used to manufacture Teladianium.

Trans-Orbital Accelerators are used to accelerate space ships to near light-speed, allowing them to quickly traverse the vast distances of the galaxy before decelerating them once more. Unlike Terran gates, they originate from the pre-quantum teleportation era and do not allow intergalactic travel.
This spatial anomaly connects distant sectors through compressed space-time corridors. Unlike the ancient gate network, wormholes possess limited energy and cannot support intergalactic travel.

This artificial spatial anomaly is generated by a Jump Hole Generator and connects distant sectors through a temporary compressed space-time corridor. Its limited stability causes the connection to eventually collapse.
This unstable one-way spatial rupture is believed to have formed during experimental gateway research.

Developed by private companies over many years, these space stations provide the highest standards of both comfort and technology.(||) Each station is fitted with bars, restaurants, casinos, holographic cinemas, shops and accommodation. Pilots can expect a friendly welcome.

This expensive device allows the user to teleport directly to any ship within range without entering open space. It also extends the range at which floating wares can be collected, allows wares to be transferred between ships, and enables ships to instantly dock at a carrier equipped with a Transporter Device. Without one aboard the carrier, instant docking is still possible if the approaching ship is equipped with a Docking Computer.

Ore Mines are mainly built around small asteroids, where lower gravity allows greater productivity. Asteroids are first analyzed with specialized scanners to determine their mineral richness.(||) Teams of robots overseen by miners operate the mines. The Ore is processed and transported to factories, where it is used to manufacture metal components. Because Terracorp holds exclusive rights to all minerals and the Commonwealth could not survive without these resources, the design of this mine has been provided free of charge to every faction. All other designs are forbidden.

Silicon Mines are built around small asteroids that are first analyzed to determine their richness in silicon minerals. The mineral is usually found just below the surface and is extracted using open-cast mining, where large earth-moving machines scrape away the asteroid's surface to expose rich bands of silicon beneath.(||) These deposits are then excavated and collected by specialized prospector robots. The Silicon is processed into thin wafers that provide raw materials for the manufacture of many technical products. Because Terracorp holds exclusive rights to all minerals and the Commonwealth could not survive without these resources, the design of this mine has been provided free of charge to every faction. All other designs are forbidden.
Chemicals are an essential resource used in manufacturing Teladianium.
Waste is produced by people and used by some industries, including Chemical Labs and, more worryingly, Protein Paste facilities.
Crystals are important for manufacturing lasers. They are produced in Crystal Fabs from Energy Cells and can also be transmuted into rare colored crystals.
Crystal Fabs produce many crystals that are used for manufacturing lasers and shields. Crystals are produced from Energy Cells.

The Chelt Aquariums that are found inside Split sectors are vast saltwater tanks kept inside geodesic domes where the Split farm the creature known as Chelts. These creatures are nourished and then culled to provide the Split with meat.(||) The skin of the Chelt is used to make a tough leather, whilst the fatty tissue, after exportation to a Rastar Refinery, is rendered down to manufacture the fine oil known as Rastar. Each Aquarium requires Energy Cells to operate the machinery that controls the giant saltwater tanks.

Chelts are sea-bound animals that once roamed the seas and oceans of the Split home planet. The Split hunted Chelts for meat, oil, and skins, which were processed into a tough leather-like material. For many jazuras, however, Chelts were overhunted and nearly driven to extinction. Today, Chelts are raised in space-based Chelt Aquariums and later sold to Rastar Refineries.

A Computer Plant manufactures both full computer systems and individual Computer Components that are in great demand throughout the universe.(||) Factories also create the more specialized computer systems found in all space ships.
Fish, Fruit, Meat, and Vegetables are all produced and consumed by Outposts.

The Hull Plating Production Facility is central to the defense industry and forms an important part of the overall economy, as demand for military ships has increased dramatically in recent years.

Production of this advanced hull plating, made from a mixture of traditional metals and Teladianium, has expanded significantly in recent years due to increased shipbuilding activity by Commonwealth forces.
Jewels, Pharmaceuticals, Seeds, and Textiles are luxury goods mostly traded by private corporations.

Jewels, Pharmaceuticals, Seeds, and Textiles are luxury goods mostly traded by private corporations.

Chip plants produce microchips, essential components in all computers. They are usually found near a computer plant, with a steady stream of transport ships traveling between the two locations.(||) The chips are manufactured from Energy Cells that are charged together to create extra conductivity. Once complete, the chips are sent on to Computer Plants for installation.
Microchips are manufactured from Energy Cells that are charged together to create extra conductivity. They are mainly used in the production process of Computer Components.
Tube Fabs manufacture Quantum Tubes, quantum-level counterparts to traditional valves. Created from Ore, they are used in the engines and control systems of all space ships.
Quantum Tubes are used in the engines and control systems of all space ships.

Ore is the most common mineral throughout the known universe. It is used in the production of almost all technical goods. Ore is produced in Ore Mines which are built around small asteroids. It can also be mined by special ships equipped with a Mobile Drilling System.

Silicon is the main mineral resource that all missiles are based on. It is usually found just below the surface of asteroids and mined in huge Silicon Mines in space, or by special ships equipped with a Mobile Drilling System.

A Rastar Refinery is a dark and evil-smelling place where large chunks of the fatty flesh of the Chelt are rendered down, and then processed to produce a fine oil called Rastar.(||) Many races use this oil as lubrication for delicate mechanical parts.

Rastar is an oil produced from the animal fat of the Chelt, a farmed sea-bound animal native to the Split.(||) Once refined, this exceptionally fine oil is used by most races to lubricate critical moving components in space stations.

A Teladianium Foundry is a large factory dedicated to producing the hard, tough material known as Teladianium, which is widely used for constructing space stations.(||) It is made by mixing dried Teladian mud with Chemicals and synthetic plastics.

Teladian mud is a very fine, silty sediment found at the bottom of rivers and swamps on the Teladi planet. When dried, it forms a hard mineral that can be mixed with Chemicals and synthetic plastics to produce Teladianium.(||) The resulting material is tough and flexible, stronger than hardened steel but considerably lighter, making it ideal for constructing space stations.

This station manufactures Advanced Satellites as replacements for the old Navigation Relay Satellites. The factory uses delicate machinery to build these sophisticated small devices.(||) With the development of information transmission through the gate network, satellites were created to boost these transmissions. Scientists later added a small sensor network to assist with navigation and long-range station management.

This satellite represents the next generation of advanced communications technology. It features video capture, a new capability developed to keep an eye on stations and ships.(||) This satellite retains the old features that allow for navigation and information relay transfer.
This undetectable equipment contains a collection of essential commands used by hackers. These commands can be accessed only from your personal ship.

This equipment allows any ST-cargo ship to manufacture a wide range of products. Although this rudimentary mobile factory is less efficient than dedicated factories, it can manufacture certain products, such as Jump Beacons and Hackerchips, more cheaply than instant crafting.

These chips were created long ago by a notorious pirate organization, after remotely hacking ships from the safety of a computer terminal became impossible. Today, these expensive pieces of hardware are still used in secret to compromise open ports on nearby ships. Their extreme energy requirements make them usable only once.

This huge station has all the necessary infrastructure to accommodate a large population and construct new ships and stations. Originally designed by Goner architects, all Outposts are built around an ingenious system of movable walls that allows new rooms to be created as needed, making the entire station highly flexible. It also has a repair bay and a ship hangar.

Originally designed by Goner architects, all Outposts are built around an ingenious system of movable walls that allows new rooms to be created as needed, making the entire station highly flexible. It also has a repair bay and a ship hangar.

Built upon the framework of a standard Outpost, this upgraded facility incorporates extensive production and docking infrastructure. Its modular architecture retains all traditional Outpost functions while providing significantly greater industrial capacity.
